title: Cross-tenant Policy Diff & Rollout Preview — Private Console UX prototype
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact, discoverable diff and rollout-preview surface in the Private Console that helps operators understand and safely apply cross-tenant network/RBAC/policy changes. The goal is a single-pane experience that shows: a) readable policy diffs scoped to affected tenants/clusters/subnets, b) simulated impact (connectivity & access paths) with a lightweight visualization, c) estimated cost delta for affected tenants after policy changes (eg. egress reroutes, new load balancer rules), and d) an integrated rollout plan composer (canary groups, time windows, auto-rollback triggers). This ticket produces a high-fidelity prototype and annotated handoff with interaction states for approval by Product and Security.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates a side-by-side unified diff view (before/after) for NetworkPolicies and RBAC bindings across selected tenants
A compact impact simulator visualizes affected pod-to-service paths and highlights blocked/allowed transitions in the preview state
Rollout composer UI allows building and saving a staged rollout (canary groups, percentage, time window) and shows expected affected hosts per stage
Estimated cost delta panel shows line items (eg. egress, LB rules, added routing) with a best-effort estimate and link to cost details dashboard
Interactions for applying, scheduling, and reversing the change are shown in prototype, with clear guardrails and confirmation flows
Design spec includes accessibility notes, microcopy for warnings/confirmations, and a security checklist to send to Security for review
notes: Motivation: ops teams are currently forced to cross-reference YAML diffs, ad-hoc scripts, and billing dashboards when making tenant-scoped policy changes. This causes two classes of mistakes: accidental wide-scoped rollouts and unexpected cost spikes.

Trade-offs considered: embedding a full topology simulator (heavy, slow) vs a lightweight probabilistic impact overlay (faster, approximate). We chose the lightweight overlay for first pass to keep SLOs intact.
Scope: this ticket covers the UX prototype and annotated interactions. Implementation of backend simulation and accurate cost modelling is tracked in ENG-55021 and ENG-55812.
